learningObjective: Distinguish weight-only, W8A8, and W4A16 quantization schemes by their memory-traffic and kernel-support profiles.
stem: Consider three inference quantization schemes: (i) weight-only INT4 with FP16 activations (W4A16), (ii) weight-only INT8 with FP16 activations (W8A16), (iii) full W8A8 (weights AND activations INT8). Which statements are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: W4A16 primarily targets memory-bandwidth-bound decode where the dominant cost is loading weights; the INT4 weights halve HBM traffic vs. INT8, and dequantization to FP16 in-register keeps the compute in FP16 Tensor Cores.
W8A8 targets compute-bound scenarios where an INT8 Tensor Core kernel is available and delivers higher TFLOPS than FP16; activations are quantized dynamically or with a calibrated static scale.
In W4A16, using an INT4 Tensor Core is required for the speedup; without INT4 Tensor Core support, the scheme cannot accelerate anything.
W8A16 is a compute-bound quantization scheme: it uses INT8 Tensor Cores for the matmul and therefore requires an activation calibration pass to determine INT8 activation scales.
For LLM decode with batch size 1, W4A16 is generally faster than W8A8 because decode is bandwidth-bound on weight loads, not compute-bound.

explanation: A: W4A16's design intent is exactly memory-bandwidth-bound decode; INT4 halves weight traffic vs. INT8 while dequant-in-register keeps compute in FP16 Tensor Cores. B: W8A8 targets compute-bound cases where INT8 Tensor Core throughput dominates and activations can be quantized cheaply. E: LLM decode at batch=1 is dominated by weight-loading bandwidth, making W4A16 typically faster than W8A8 despite W8A8's compute advantage. C is false: W4A16 GEMMs dequant INT4 to FP16 in registers and use FP16 Tensor Cores — INT4 Tensor Core support is not required. D is false: W8A16 is weight-only quantization; activations stay in FP16 so no activation-calibration step is needed and the matmul uses FP16 Tensor Cores (with dequantized weights), not INT8.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: W4A16 memory-bandwidth logic and dequant-in-register.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: W4A16 does not require INT4 Tensor Cores.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: W8A16 is weight-only — activations stay in FP16, no activation calibration needed, matmul uses FP16 TCs.

assumptions: The GPU has FP16 Tensor Core support (Ampere or newer).
The kernel available for W4A16 performs dequant-in-register (typical of Marlin, ExLlama, gptq_gemm).
nonImplications: Does not imply W4A16 beats W8A8 for large-batch prefill (compute-bound); W8A8 can win there.
Does not imply weight-only quantization has zero accuracy cost; it depends on calibration method (RTN, GPTQ, AWQ).

distractorRationales.C: Fabricates a Tensor Core precision requirement.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses weight-only W8A16 with W8A8; the '16' in A16 means FP16 activations.

performanceClaim.scope: Comparative use cases of W4A16 vs W8A8 vs W8A16 on GPU
